card.summary: The Federal Correctional Officer Paycheck Protection Act of 2026 aims to improve recruitment and retention of Federal correctional officers by increasing their base rates of pay by 35 percent. The bill applies to certain employees of the Bureau of Prisons whose duties relate to the custody, control, or supervision of inmates or who have routine direct inmate contact. It also includes certain prevailing rate employees up to grade 9 of the Federal Wage System. The pay increases are subject to a 5-year sunset period unless the Department of Justice Inspector General determines that the Bureau of Prisons has made measurable progress in eliminating augmentation and reducing excessive mandatory overtime.

summary: The Federal Correctional Officer Paycheck Protection Act of 2026 aims to improve the recruitment and retention of federal correctional officers by increasing their base rates of pay. It establishes a 35 percent pay increase for certain Bureau of Prisons employees, subject to a five-year sunset unless specific progress is made regarding staffing and overtime.

affected_groups.effect: Receive a 35 percent increase to their base rates of pay or wage rates, subject to certain salary caps and a five-year sunset provision.
affected_groups.group: Federal correctional officers and certain Bureau of Prisons employees

affected_groups.effect: Required to review the Bureau of Prisons' progress on reducing augmentation and mandatory overtime and report to Congress before the end of the five-year period.

key_provisions: Establishes special base rates of pay for federal correctional officers employed by the Bureau of Prisons who primarily relate to the custody, control, or supervision of inmates.
Computes the special base rate by increasing the applicable General Schedule base rate or LEO special base rate by 35 percent, capped at level V of the Executive Schedule.

Requires the Attorney General to increase wage rates by 35 percent for certain covered prevailing rate employees classified not higher than grade 9 of the Federal Wage System, capped at level IV of the Executive Schedule.
Sets a five-year sunset date on the pay authorities created by the Act, causing them to terminate and repeal unless continued.

Directs the Inspector General of the Department of Justice to conduct a review and report to Congress 180 days before the five-year expiration regarding augmentation, mandatory overtime, recruitment, retention, and safety.

Allows the pay authorities to continue past five years if the Inspector General determines the Bureau of Prisons has demonstrated measurable progress in eliminating augmentation and reducing excessive mandatory overtime.

summary_detail.significance: This bill modifies the compensation structure for federal correctional officers within the Bureau of Prisons by providing a 35 percent pay increase. The potential significance depends on whether the pay increase helps with recruitment and retention, reduces mandatory overtime, and leads to the permanent continuation of the pay authorities after the five-year review by the Inspector General.
